properties.areaDesc: Straits of Florida from west end of Seven Mile Bridge to south of Halfmoon Shoal 20 to 60 NM out
properties.headline: Marine Weather Statement issued October 24 at 9:58AM EDT by NWS Key West FL
properties.description:
The areas affected include...
Straits of Florida from west end of Seven Mile Bridge to south of
Halfmoon Shoal 20 to 60 nm out...

At 958 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated a a strong thunderstorm,
capable of producing wind gusts near 30 knots. This thunderstorm was
located 40 nm south of Wood's Wall West Crack, moving southwest at 10
knots.

The strong thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.
properties.instruction:
Prepare for thunderstorms with wind gusts near 30 knots, locally
rough and confused seas, occasional lightning strikes, and
potentially blinding downpours. Get to a safe port as quickly, and as
safely as possible. When downpours reduce visibility, slow down.

NWSheadline: A STRONG THUNDERSTORM OVER THE WATERS

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 24 at 9:52AM EDT until October 25 at 2:00PM EDT by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in southeast
Georgia...

Satilla River At Atkinson affecting Brantley County.

Additional information is available at
https://water.weather.gov/wfo/JAX

The next statement will be issued Sunday morning at 1000 AM EDT.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Satilla River at Atkinson.

* WHEN...Until Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 13.0 feet, Warners Landing, Louis Landing and
secondary roads around KOA campgrounds begin to flood. At 14.0
feet, River Rock Road begins to experience flooding across the
road.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:45 AM EDT Saturday the stage was 13.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage
tomorrow morning and continue falling to 11.7 feet Thursday
morning.
- Flood stage is 13.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 24 at 5:30AM AKDT until October 27 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding is
possible with water levels between 2 to 4 feet above the normal
high tide line. For the High Surf Advisory, water levels
between 1 to 3 ft above the normal high tide line. For the
Coastal Flood Watch, more significant coastal flooding possible
around Monday night. Water Levels between 4 and 6 feet are
possible.

* WHERE...Shishmaref.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 10 PM AKDT
Sunday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 10 PM Sunday to 4 AM
AKDT Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late Monday
night through late Tuesday night.

* IMPACTS...Minor coastal flooding is possible. Some shoreline
erosion may occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Water levels up to 4 feet in Shishmaref
may result in erosion on the road to the landfill with high
water in the lagoon.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Precautions should be taken to protect property.

* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Minor coastal flooding

tide line expected.For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 2 to 4 ft.

* WHERE...Southern Seward Peninsula Coast.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM AKDT Sunday.
For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 PM Sunday to 4 AM AKDT
Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...For Nome and Golovin, water levels have peaked and
will begin to gradually drop on Saturday. While water levels
remain near their apex, in Nome, this can result in water
approaching low- lying homes in Belmont Subdivision with
standing water expected in the port area. For Golovin, water may
inundate any beach property but the roads, buildings and
residences shouldn't be impacted as the water remains below the
berm. Even though water levels drop somewhat, they will remain
normal through early next week. Localized beach erosion may
occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...South to southwest winds will continue to
gust up to 40 mph through the weekend. Strong winds continue
into early next week

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 24 at 9:15AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Persistent northeast winds have caused river levels on the St Johns
at Astor to rise into Moderate Flood Stage. The river is forecast to
climb slowly through Moderate Flood Stage through the weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog and Bonnet roads become inaccessible with several
inches of water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at
Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged.
Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards
completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded
in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on Juno
Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Saturday the stage was 3.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EDT Saturday was 3.2 feet.
- Forecast...A gradual rise is forecast this weekend into early
next week, remaining in Moderate Flood Stage.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EDT.

properties.areaDesc: Richmond; Lancaster; Middlesex; Mathews; Western Essex; Eastern Essex
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 24 at 9:04AM EDT until October 24 at 2:00PM EDT by NWS Wakefield VA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to one foot of inundation above ground level in
low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Richmond, Lancaster, Middlesex, Mathews, Western Essex
and Eastern Essex Counties.

* WHEN...Until 2 PM EDT this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Shallow flooding is expected in the most vulnerable
locations near the waterfront and shoreline resulting in a low
threat of property damage. Expect up to one foot of water
above ground level in low lying, vulnerable areas. Some roads
and low lying property including parking lots, parks and lawns
near the waterfront will experience shallow flooding.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.
